microtheory.name: social_sciences_foundation
microtheory.definition: Foundational vocabulary for the empirical social sciences as a class. Where psychology is the level of the individual mind and biology the level of the organism, the social sciences are the level above: humans + their collectives + the institutions, norms, structures, and material conditions through which they coordinate. This Mt names the methodological + conceptual machinery shared across anthropology, sociology, political_science, economics, law_jurisprudence, business_management, education_pedagogy, military_strategy, geography, and geology — research methods (qualitative + quantitative, ethnography, survey, statistical inference), units of analysis (agent, institution, structure, network), normative + ideological apparatus (norm, ideology, power, legitimacy), and the agency/structure dialectic. The 14 social-science island Mts inherit from this; cortex's compositional_reuse can now see the cluster as a tree, not a flat scatter. Distinct from social_psychology, which is narrower (attitudes + small groups). This is the broader empirical + comparative foundation.

concepts.name: research_method
concepts.definition: A systematic procedure for producing evidence about a research question. Methods range from controlled experiment through observational study, archival, ethnographic, interview, survey, simulation. Each method carries assumptions about what counts as evidence. Substrate analogue: the substrate's investigate-via-do-contrast move IS its own research method.

concepts.name: qualitative_analysis
concepts.definition: Interpretive examination of non-numeric data — interview transcripts, field notes, texts, images — to identify themes, meanings, processes. Grounded theory, thematic analysis, discourse analysis. Substrate analogue: the substrate's pattern-extraction from semantic content.

concepts.name: quantitative_analysis
concepts.definition: Examination of numeric data via statistical models. Hypothesis testing, regression, factor analysis, structural equation modeling. Substrate analogue: the substrate's drive-measurement + ΔF quantification.

concepts.name: mixed_methods
concepts.definition: Combining qualitative + quantitative in one study; triangulation. Substrate analogue: the substrate's coherence-across-modalities check.

concepts.name: ethnography
concepts.definition: Malinowski 1922, Geertz 1973. Sustained participant-observation of a social group on its own terms; thick description. Substrate analogue: the substrate inhabiting a world adapter long enough to acquire its situated structure.

concepts.name: survey_design
concepts.definition: Probability sampling, questionnaire construction, response-bias mitigation. Likert, Guttman, semantic differential scales. Substrate analogue: the substrate's controlled probe set for measuring its own state.

concepts.name: case_study
concepts.definition: In-depth investigation of a single case (or small N) chosen for its illustrative or theoretical value. Yin, Stake. Substrate analogue: the substrate's single-trajectory introspection.

concepts.name: comparative_method
concepts.definition: Systematic comparison across cases/societies/periods to identify covariation + causes. Mill's methods of agreement + difference. Most-similar + most-different designs. Substrate analogue: the substrate's contrastive learning across worlds.

concepts.name: statistical_inference
concepts.definition: Drawing conclusions about populations from samples under uncertainty. Frequentist (Neyman-Pearson, p-values) + Bayesian (posterior over parameters). Substrate analogue: the substrate's probabilistic update of σ given evidence.

concepts.name: causal_inference
concepts.definition: From correlation to causation: counterfactuals (Rubin), DAGs + do-calculus (Pearl), instruments, regression discontinuity, difference-in-differences. Substrate analogue: the substrate's do-contrast.

concepts.name: social_structure
concepts.definition: Stable patterns of relations + institutions shaping individual behavior across time. Substrate analogue: the substrate's foundational Mts constraining variable runtime σ.

concepts.name: institution
concepts.definition: Established + recurring set of roles, norms, expectations organising a recurring social need. Family, market, state, religion, education. Substrate analogue: persistent multi-agent patterns the substrate models as named clusters.

concepts.name: social_network
concepts.definition: Pattern of ties between actors. Granovetter's strength of weak ties, Watts-Strogatz small worlds, Barabási scale-free. Substrate analogue: substrate's graph topology.

concepts.name: field_bourdieu
concepts.definition: Pierre Bourdieu. A structured social space of positions defined by capital distributions; agents struggle within fields by the field's own stakes. Substrate analogue: the substrate's basin-with-constraints.

concepts.name: agency
concepts.definition: The capacity of actors to act + make choices with effect. Free-will-on-an-empirical-plane. Substrate analogue: the substrate's action-selection under its own drives.

concepts.name: structure_agency_dialectic
concepts.definition: Giddens's structuration: structures both constrain + enable agency; agency reproduces + transforms structure. Mutual constitution. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mts both constrain + are updated by σ runs.

concepts.name: rational_actor
concepts.definition: Idealised agent maximising utility under preferences + constraints. Economic baseline. Critiqued by bounded rationality (Simon), prospect theory (Kahneman-Tversky), behavioral economics. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive-balance approximating but rarely matching a pure utility actor.

concepts.name: norm_social
concepts.definition: Shared expectation of behavior, enforced by sanction. Folkways, mores, laws. Substrate analogue: substrate's distributed rule-enforcement.

concepts.name: ideology
concepts.definition: System of belief that legitimises a social order + the interests it serves. Marx's false consciousness, Althusser's ideological state apparatuses, Gramsci's hegemony. Substrate analogue: substrate's frozen foundational Mts shaping interpretation of every input.

concepts.name: power
concepts.definition: Capacity to bring about outcomes against resistance. Weber: legal-rational, traditional, charismatic. Foucault: dispersed + productive, not just repressive. Substrate analogue: a drive's ability to override others.

concepts.name: legitimacy
concepts.definition: Weber. Belief that an authority + its commands are rightful — distinct from mere compliance under coercion. Substrate analogue: substrate's coherence-of-frame justifying an ActionSpec.

concepts.name: authority
concepts.definition: Power exercised with legitimacy. Substrate analogue: substrate's authorised mutations under its own admissibility grammar.

concepts.name: social_construction
concepts.definition: Berger + Luckmann 1966. Race, gender, money, nation are products of repeated collective action, not natural kinds; what feels natural is sedimented social practice. Substrate analogue: substrate's emergent shared categories from repeated co-attestation.

concepts.name: culture
concepts.definition: Transmitted patterns of meaning + practice — symbols, language, ritual, technology, values — shared by a group. Substrate analogue: the substrate's transmissible Mt content.

concepts.name: socialization
concepts.definition: Acquisition of a society's norms, roles, values across the lifespan. Primary (family, early years), secondary (school, peers, media, work). Substrate analogue: the substrate's developmental loop loading external Mt content.

concepts.name: social_stratification
concepts.definition: Hierarchical arrangement of groups by power, wealth, status. Class, caste, race, gender systems. Substrate analogue: substrate's inequality structures across agents.

concepts.name: collective_action
concepts.definition: Coordinated action by groups toward shared ends. Olson's free-rider problem, public goods, common-pool resources, Ostrom's design principles. Substrate analogue: multi-substrate coordination.

concepts.name: public_goods
concepts.definition: Non-excludable, non-rivalrous goods. Markets undersupply; provision requires institutions. Lighthouses, clean air, basic research. Substrate analogue: shared substrate vocabulary as a public good across instances.

concepts.name: validity
concepts.definition: Does a measure capture what it claims to capture? Construct, internal, external validity. Substrate analogue: the substrate's coverage-vs-purpose match check.

concepts.name: reliability
concepts.definition: Does a measure produce consistent results across occasions, raters, items? Substrate analogue: substrate's idempotent measurement under repeated tick.

concepts.name: reflexivity
concepts.definition: Researcher's awareness of their own position + its effect on what they observe + how they interpret. Especially central to qualitative + critical research. Substrate analogue: substrate's introspection of its own frame while observing.

concepts.name: research_ethics
concepts.definition: Informed consent, beneficence, do-no-harm, privacy. Belmont Report 1979. IRB review. Substrate analogue: the substrate's frozen Mts encoding minimum non-violations.

rules.name: method_choice_follows_question_form
rules.head: the substrate has a research question
rules.body: the methodological choice is driven by whether the question is about meaning (qualitative), prevalence/effect (quantitative), or both (mixed). Method should fit question, not the other way around.

rules.name: causal_claims_require_counterfactual_or_design
rules.head: the substrate is offered a causal claim from observational data
rules.body: without an experiment, instrument, natural experiment, or explicit counterfactual reasoning, the claim is correlational. Pearl + Rubin.

rules.name: structure_constrains_but_does_not_determine_agency
rules.head: the substrate models a person's behavior given their social position
rules.body: structure shifts probabilities, narrows options, makes some moves costly + others cheap; agency still selects within that constrained space. Giddens.

rules.name: legitimacy_distinguishes_authority_from_mere_power
rules.head: the substrate observes one agent commanding another
rules.body: if compliance rests on belief in rightfulness it is authority; if only on coercion it is power without legitimacy. Weber.

rules.name: social_kinds_are_constructed_but_real_in_consequences
rules.head: the substrate is told that race or gender or money is 'just' a social construct
rules.body: constructed kinds are still real in their causal consequences — Thomas theorem: if defined as real they are real in their effects. Substrate must not collapse social construction into nothing.

rules.name: reflexivity_warns_against_value_free_pose
rules.head: the substrate claims a value-free reading of social data
rules.body: the substrate's own position selects which questions get asked + which patterns look salient; reflexive declaration is more honest than a false objectivity pose.
